title: Annotatio II §.VIII open PERDURATIO: Seemed extinct — Waldenses not consub; revived by John of Paris
pass_a_gloss: §. VIII. Although by this pact Consubstantiation seemed extinct — taught for a short enough time and by rather few; the Waldenses also (in whose doctrine of the Sacred Supper some boast a subtler Consubstantiation sentence preserved) professing something altogether different from Consubstantiation, which our fourth Annotation will show to the eye — yet it was resuscitated as if from the dead by right of return, toward the end of the aforesaid 13th Century, by John of Paris, a Monk of the Dominican order.
pass_b_english: §.VIII PERDURATIO: Consubstantiation looked extinct — short-lived, few teachers; Waldenses (some claim) keep a subtler line, but they actually teach something else (see Annotatio IV).
Yet it rose again near the end of the 13th century through John of Paris, Dominican.
source_text: §. VIII. Etsi verò hoc pacto extincta visa est Consubstantiatio, exiguo satis tempore & à paucioribus edocta; Waldensibus etiam (in quorum doctrina de S. Coena, Consubstantiationis subtilioris sententiam conservatam nonnulli gloriantur) diversum prorsus à Consubstantiatione profitentibus, id quod Annotatio nostra quarta ad oculum ostendet; tamen resuscitata quasi è mortuis postliminio fuit, sub finem Seculi supra dicti XIII., per Johannem Parisienfem, Monachum ex ordine Dominicano.

lemmas.gloss: resuscitated as if from the dead

choices.english: by right of return / from exile

notes: §.VIII open; extinct then John of Paris revival.
